title: Select project license and identify the canonical GitHub repository
description:
## Decision

The maintainer must select the canonical SPDX license, provide the exact GitHub repository URL, and confirm whether boss@fullofcaffeine.com is the intended published confidential security channel.

## Rationale

License intent cannot be inferred from neighboring projects, and GitHub security controls cannot be verified or changed without an unambiguous repository identity. Publishing an unapproved email or guessed license would be irreversible public policy.

## Alternatives Considered

- MIT, matching genes-ts and Next.js.
- GPL-3.0-only, matching several sibling Haxe backend projects.
- Another maintainer-selected SPDX license with explicit rationale.
- Existing email reporting, verified GitHub private vulnerability reporting, or both.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- The maintainer names one canonical SPDX license.
- The exact GitHub owner/repository or URL is recorded.
- The maintainer confirms or replaces the published security email.
- Any explicit host-control risk acceptance is recorded.

title: Finalize license and repository-host public security controls
description: Before changing repository visibility, select the canonical project license and verify the hosting controls that cannot be proven from a local checkout: private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning and push protection, Dependabot alerts/security updates, least-privilege Actions defaults, and protected default-branch policy. Keep package metadata, README, SECURITY.md, and release policy aligned with the actual decisions and configured repository state.
design: Local and repository-host responsibilities are separate. The repository must carry one maintainer-selected SPDX license consistently in LICENSE, package metadata, README, and later artifacts. GitHub controls must be verified against the exact repository rather than inferred from workflow files: private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning and push protection, Dependabot alerts and security updates, default Actions permissions, and protected default-branch rules. The workflow keeps explicit contents: read permissions and Dependabot configuration in Git, while host settings remain external evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A canonical license is selected by the maintainer and LICENSE, package metadata, README, and distribution notices agree.
- A verified private vulnerability-reporting path is enabled and SECURITY.md points to the real confidential channel.
- Repository secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts/security updates, least-privilege Actions defaults, and default-branch protection are enabled or an explicit risk decision is recorded.
- The complete Git and Beads/Dolt histories pass the public preflight immediately before the visibility change.
- No open P0/P1 public-readiness blocker remains when visibility changes.
notes:
Local audit: no LICENSE file exists; the root package has no license field; README explicitly says the license is not final. genes-ts and Next.js use MIT, while the nearby haxe.c, haxe.ruby, and haxe.elixir.codex backends use GPL-3.0 variants, so maintainer intent cannot be inferred safely. SECURITY.md currently publishes boss@fullofcaffeine.com and treats future GitHub private vulnerability reporting as unverified. Governance workflows declare contents: read, pin Actions by full SHA, scan secrets, and audit dependencies; .github/dependabot.yml covers npm and GitHub Actions weekly. The checkout has no Git remote or upstream branch, so no exact GitHub repository or host setting can be inspected; mandatory pull and push attempts failed for that reason. The latest public preflight passed before this audit. Needed from maintainer: canonical license, exact GitHub repository identifier, and confirmation that the published security email is the intended confidential channel.
Human decision dependency created: nxhx-f34.1.8.1. F08 resumes after the license, repository identity, and security channel are supplied.

title: Implement route-segment parser and dynamic param validator
description:
Parse static, dynamic, catch-all, optional catch-all, and supported route-group syntax; derive public URL patterns and validate Haxe param typedefs/codecs.

Planning alias: NXHX-A04
PRD sections: 11.3
design: Implement A04 as a closed P0 route-pattern model under nextjshx.route. A pure parser accepts only root/static, [name], [...name], and [[...name]] segments; derives the leading-slash public pattern; preserves ordered parameter cardinality; rejects absolute/backslash/empty/traversal/control/private/file-shaped paths, malformed or duplicate parameters, and non-terminal catch-alls before generation. Per accepted ADR 0002, route groups are deferred rather than silently stripped, and groups, @slots, and interception markers receive distinct stable diagnostics. A macro boundary attaches parse failures to the declaration metadata position and validates an exact anonymous Haxe params shape: String or a transitively string-backed abstract for single segments, Array<String> for catch-all, and required genes.ts.Undefinable<Array<String>> for optional catch-all. A non-string-backed domain abstract is accepted only with one @:next.routeCodec(Type) whose fully qualified class exposes public static decode(String):T and encode(T):String; validated bindings retain the codec identity for downstream adapters/href generation. Focused no-output fixtures snapshot positive root/static/dynamic/catch-all/optional/domain/codec patterns in canonical order and assert exact source-positioned failures for traversal, reserved/private paths, malformed/deferred syntax, duplicates/placement, missing/extra/wrong fields, and invalid/missing codecs. Rendering, href runtime generation, route-pattern collision across declarations, and App Router publication remain downstream.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- [id], [...slug], and [[...slug]] positive fixtures pass.
- Missing/extra/wrong param types fail with source-positioned diagnostics.
- Traversal/reserved/malformed paths fail before generation.
- Unsupported slots/interception syntax is rejected explicitly.
notes: Implemented a closed P0 route model under nextjshx.route. The pure parser derives root and leading-slash public patterns for static, dynamic, required catch-all, and optional catch-all segments; rejects absolute, traversal, private, non-portable, file-shaped, malformed, duplicate, and misplaced paths before output; and reports deferred route groups, slots, and interception markers distinctly. The macro validator requires exact anonymous params fields, String or safe String-backed abstracts, Array<String>, genes.ts.Undefinable<Array<String>>, or a structurally validated fully qualified route codec. Validated bindings retain ordered cardinality, source segment index, Haxe identity, and codec identity for downstream adapters and hrefs. Evidence on Haxe 4.3.7 and genes-ts 1.32.0 at 1e7e323fdbda4c5b93689355294bd978e9170725: npm run test:routes passed seven canonical forward/reverse positives, the reviewed snapshot, no JavaScript output, no host paths, and 18 exact source-positioned fail-closed diagnostics. npm run public:preflight passed formatting, whitespace, Git and decoded-Beads Gitleaks, 161 tracked-text path checks, zero-vulnerability audit, every harness layer, strict TypeScript, Next 16.2.10 typegen/build, and GET smoke.
close_reason: Completed the closed route grammar, exact params and codec validation, deterministic no-output evidence, documentation, and full public-preflight verification.

design: Define a closed, schema-v1 compile-time model under nextjshx.adapter plus a checked-in JSON Schema and fixed-order encoder. AdapterPlanRegistry installs one after-typing finalizer, converts Haxe positions to repository-relative portable ranges, validates and canonicalizes each intent, sorts complete intents by target/kind/source, rejects duplicate targets before creating directories or writing plan bytes, and emits JSON only. A focused macro fixture registers the same real typed declarations in forward and reverse order; the test requires byte-identical output, JSON-Schema validity, an exact reviewed snapshot, stable source positions, and no application runtime output. A duplicate-target fixture must emit one exact source-positioned diagnostic while preserving sentinel plan bytes. Rendering, live App Router publication, ownership manifests, route-pattern conflicts, and kind-specific signature checks remain with their owning downstream Beads.
acceptance_criteria:

- Duplicate targets are rejected during plan validation.
- Every intent retains a Haxe source position for diagnostics.
- Plan can be emitted as JSON for tests/tooling without executing app code.
notes: Implemented the closed adapter-plan schema v1 and macro registry under nextjshx.adapter. The fixed-order encoder and UTF-8 bytewise canonicalization produce identical JSON bytes from forward/reverse registration order. Every intent retains repository-relative Haxe type, field, and metadata ranges; path, nested-collection, kind, and literal-config validation fails closed. Duplicate targets emit exact NXHX-PLAN-DUPLICATE-0001 diagnostics before directory/file writes and preserve pre-existing plan bytes. The fixture uses --no-output and a throwing main to prove plan generation neither emits nor executes application JavaScript. Evidence on Haxe 4.3.7, genes-ts 1.32.0 at 1e7e323fdbda4c5b93689355294bd978e9170725, Next 16.2.10, and Node 20.19.3: npm run test:adapter-plan passed schema/Ajv boundary mutations, canonical snapshot, portable ranges, no host-path leaks, and duplicate failure; npm test passed all harness, packed-consumer, dual genes output, strict TypeScript, Next typegen/build, and HTTP smoke gates; npm run public:preflight passed exact Haxe formatting, tracked whitespace, Git/decoded-Beads Gitleaks, 130 tracked text path checks, zero-vulnerability npm audit, and the complete suite.
close_reason: Completed schema-v1 adapter-plan modeling, deterministic emission, source-position retention, fail-closed duplicate detection, and no-runtime focused/public-preflight evidence.

Planning alias: NXHX-G04

design: Adopt the existing generic external-caller policies rather than adding a new compiler primitive. Application-local authored JS/TS imports require explicit Haxe module discovery plus narrow @:keep. Published public graphs use @:genes.library with -D genes.library and matched classic declarations. Prove precise component handles and both output profiles without disabling DCE or retaining unrelated modules.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A generic fixture reproduces TS-only import visibility.
- The supported keep/export pattern is documented.
- Component type remains precise under strict TSX checking.
- Classic JS behavior is unchanged or explicitly guarded.
- Full genes-ts CI passes for compiler changes.
notes: Completed by NextJsHx commit 7de4c048f79c550c0d89f23cf006e7454efe51eb without a genes-ts compiler change. The framework-neutral compiler-gap corpus proves an explicitly discovered @:keep external entry remains precisely typed in TypeScript and classic JS/declarations while an unmarked negative control stays absent under full DCE. docs/compiler-gap-inventory.md and the stable fixture README distinguish application-local package inclusion plus narrow @:keep from the published-library @:genes.library/-D genes.library policy. The stable Next fixture imports HelloView only from authored TypeScript, contains no fake Haxe reachability call or broad cast, and passes strict TypeScript with skipLibCheck false. Fresh evidence on Node 20.19.3, Haxe 4.3.7, genes-ts 1.32.0, and Next 16.2.10: npm run test:compiler-gaps passed both output profiles; next typegen, strict tsc, Turbopack production build, and GET / smoke passed; npm run public:preflight passed Haxe formatting, whitespace, Git/decoded-Beads gitleaks, zero-vulnerability npm audit, all harness layers, package shape, production build, and runtime smoke.
close_reason: Verified and documented the existing DCE-safe external-caller policies in generic TypeScript/classic fixtures and a strict production Next component import; no additional Genes primitive or broad retention is needed.

title: Write ADR: public namespace and App Router authoring syntax
description:
## Decision

Select and document the public namespace split and initial App Router authoring syntax for pages, layouts, route handlers, client components, and Server Functions.

## Rationale

The API must preserve a faithful raw Next.js escape hatch while adding typed Haxe ergonomics without creating a duplicated central route registry.

## Alternatives Considered

- Raw externs only, with no semantic layer.
- Semantic wrappers only, hiding the public Next.js surface.
- A central manually maintained route declaration list.

Planning alias: NXHX-F04
PRD sections: 8.3, 10, 11, 12
design: Accepted ADR 0002: docs/adr/0002-public-namespace-and-app-router-authoring.md (indexed by docs/architecture.md). Public API split: nextjs.raw.* faithful allowlisted Next façades; nextjs.* supported semantic APIs and compile-time authoring; nextjs._internal.* unstable declaration support; nextjshx.* tooling internals. Initial App Router syntax is one annotated app-owned class per page, layout, Route Handler, client boundary, or dedicated Server Function module, with explicit adapter-root-relative paths, fixed typed export conventions, per-route href helpers, ClientComponent.ref and ServerFunction.ref boundary imports, deterministic source discovery, and no manually maintained central route registry. Advanced route syntax and additional special-file annotations remain explicitly deferred pending dedicated evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- ADR includes representative Haxe and generated TS examples.
- The design preserves a faithful raw escape hatch.
- The design avoids a central manually duplicated route list.
- Unsupported future syntax is explicitly deferred.
close_reason: NXHX-F04 complete: accepted ADR 0002 (docs/adr/0002-public-namespace-and-app-router-authoring.md) and indexed it from docs/architecture.md and the ADR catalog. The decision locks the nextjs.raw.*, nextjs.*, nextjs._internal.*, and nextjshx.* responsibilities; one annotated app-owned class per page, layout, Route Handler, client boundary, or dedicated Server Function module; explicit App-Router-root-relative paths; fixed typed field/export conventions; per-route href helpers; ClientComponent.ref and ServerFunction.ref boundary imports; deterministic declaration discovery; and no manually maintained route registry. It includes representative Haxe and generated TypeScript/TSX for every selected boundary, preserves native TypeScript and raw façades as escape hatches, compares four rejected alternatives, and explicitly defers advanced syntax. Added fail-closed ADR integrity requirements. Verification: npm test; npm run test:architecture; six generated TypeScript/TSX examples parsed with TypeScript 6.0.2; bd dep cycles; bd graph check; bd lint; seed checksums; whitespace and diff checks.

title: Write ADR: adapter-first App Router integration
description:
## Decision

Select and document the canonical App Router integration strategy. The current recommendation is adapter-first generation with explicit criteria for any future direct genes-ts emission.

## Rationale

Next requires exact filenames, default and named exports, and directive placement that a file-per-Haxe-module compiler cannot reliably express without a narrow adapter layer.

## Alternatives Considered

- Generic direct compiler emission for directives and export shapes.
- A custom runtime or router that replaces Next conventions.
- Hand-maintained TypeScript adapters without generated ownership.

Planning alias: NXHX-F03
PRD sections: 9
design: Accepted ADR 0001: docs/adr/0001-adapter-first-app-router-integration.md (indexed by docs/architecture.md). Canonical strategy: deterministic, narrow, manifest-owned Next-native adapters bridge genes-ts implementation modules to exact App Router paths, directives, exports, and Next-generated type helpers. A specific adapter kind may move to direct genes-ts emission only through reviewed ADR evidence satisfying the recorded generic-compiler, type-oracle, DCE, stable-fixture, and ownership criteria. F05's hand-written adapter is an explicitly temporary integration proof.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- ADR compares adapter-first, direct compiler emission, and custom runtime alternatives.
- ADR selects adapter-first and explains directives/default exports/filesystem constraints.
- ADR defines files NextJsHx never owns.
- Decision is linked from the architecture docs and relevant Beads.
close_reason: NXHX-F03 complete: accepted ADR 0001 (docs/adr/0001-adapter-first-app-router-integration.md) and linked it from docs/architecture.md, the ADR index, README, CONTRIBUTING, and the Bead design field. The decision makes narrow deterministic manifest-owned Next-native adapters canonical; explains exact filesystem, default/named export, directive-placement, Next type-oracle, and file-level ownership constraints; includes page, client-boundary, Server Function, and Route Handler examples; defines files NextJsHx never owns implicitly; compares direct genes-ts emission, custom runtime/router, hand-maintained adapters, and extern-only alternatives; and establishes ten evidence criteria for any future direct-emission replacement. Added an ADR integrity checker to pre-commit, root tests, and CI. Verification: npm run test:architecture; npm test; npm run public:preflight; bd dep cycles; bd graph check; bd lint; seed checksums. Results: 1 accepted ADR indexed, 0 npm vulnerabilities, and 0 Gitleaks findings across staged content, reachable Git history, and 13.50 MB decoded Beads history.

title: Write ContractHx architecture ADR and transport profile model
description:
## Decision

Select or reject a transport-neutral ContractHx architecture and first transport profile after comparing the available native-framework options.

## Rationale

Any shared contract must remove duplicated wire declarations without replacing Next, Phoenix, or Rails runtime semantics or forcing local Next Server Functions through RPC.

## Alternatives Considered

- HTTP JSON with generated native adapters.
- Next Server Functions as a universal transport.
- Phoenix Channels or LiveView as the shared protocol.
- Rails ActionCable or Hotwire as the shared protocol.
- OpenAPI-first generation.
